title: Jonah and the Thorn
premise: Sable Coldharbour, a memory-thief who keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Debt—a guild that trades in impossible things—has spent his life making himself forgettable to survive. But when the old gods wake and begin answering prayers, the debts in his ledgers start collecting themselves, and one entry bears his own name: a soul he sold to the court beneath the mountain to buy his sister's life. To reclaim it, Sable must steal back what was never his to sell, aided by Wren, a priestess of the waking god who loves him against her vows. In the end, Sable learns the soul he seeks is his own past self—the memories he carved out to become invisible—and he must choose between restoring the man he was and remaining the hollow, safe thief he became. He chooses wholeness, pays the thorn-price the gods demand, and walks into the light remembered.
about_author: Jude Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction about the things we refuse to remember. They write fantasy from a drafty house on the coast, where the fog does most of the worldbuilding.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He balances the Gilded Debt's books, trading stolen memories for coin and staying deliberately unremarkable. A routine entry—his sister's soul-price—begins to glow with new ink that wasn't there yesterday. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a man whose invisibility is failing.

chapters.title: Prayers with Teeth
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Old gods answer a beggar's prayer in the guild's own courtyard, and the Debt's clients panic. The guildmaster orders Sable to erase all records touching the divine. He discovers the glowing entry names him as debtor. Emotional beat: vertigo as the safe walls of anonymity crack.

chapters.title: Wren at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A young priestess of the waking god is sent to investigate the guild's divine debts. She interviews Sable and senses the hollow where his memories were cut away. Emotional beat: recognition between two people who both serve something they fear.

chapters.title: What the Sister Paid
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He confronts his sister Maren, alive but strangely faded, and learns the truth: to buy her cure, he sold not memories but his soul's first self to the court beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: grief and self-betrayal; the thief learns he robbed himself.

chapters.title: The Price of the Thorn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren breaks her vows to help Sable, consulting her god directly and receiving a warning: wholeness has a thorn-price, pain freely chosen. They grow closer, and she chooses him over her order. Emotional beat: love kindling against duty, both knowing the cost.

chapters.title: Descent by Ledger-Light
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Guided by his own bookkeeping, Sable and Wren descend toward the court beneath the mountain, trading memories at each gate as toll. Sable gives away pieces of himself willingly for the first time. Emotional beat: a miser learning generosity, terror and wonder entwined.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the subterranean court, the old gods sit in judgment over debts of the soul. Sable finds his sold self—a boy who still remembers their mother's face—kept as a court favorite. Emotional beat: heartbreak at meeting the person he erased.

chapters.title: A Theft in Two Directions
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. While Sable distracts the court with a false ledger, Wren attempts the theft of the boy-soul. She is caught; the court offers her a bargain—Sable's debt forgiven in exchange for her god's name. Emotional beat: duty and love collide at knife-point.

chapters.title: The Thorn Takes Root
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Climax. Sable refuses the easy trade and instead merges with his sold self, accepting the thorn-price: he will feel everything he once cut away, forever. The court, bound by its own law, must release him. Emotional beat: agonizing, triumphant reclamation of identity.

chapters.title: Remembered
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Above ground, Sable—whole, aching, visible at last—burns the ledger entry bearing his name. Maren brightens; Wren, exiled but unregretful, stands beside him as the old gods' new age begins. Emotional beat: resolution—the price of survival paid, and love chosen over invisibility.
